ai.title: Switch Discord integration to Gateway API
ai.summary: Discord bot logic migrated from Interactions API to Gateway API using discord.js. New `web/scripts/discord/index.ts` starts the client, while `register-commands.ts` handles slash command registration via REST. Removed dependency on `discord-interactions` and deleted the Next.js API route `web/src/app/api/discord/interactions/route.ts`. Rate limiter moved to `web/src/discord/rate-limiter.ts`.

eli5.text: The Discord bot that helps link your Discord account to your Codebuff account has been rebuilt from the ground up to use Discord's newer, more reliable connection method. Previously, the bot relied on a separate service that handled interactions differently; now, it connects directly to Discord using an updated library, and the old connection method along with its supporting setup files have been removed. If you notice anything, it might be a slightly smoother experience when using the bot, though the basic functions, like running the '/link' command to connect your accounts, should work just as before. This change is internal and mostly affects how the bot operates behind the scenes.

ai.title: Reword knowledge files system prompt
ai.summary: Updated `knowledgeFilesPrompt` in `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts`. Clarified file creation context, consolidated update triggers, and tightened inclusion/exclusion lists. Scope limited to backend system prompt logic.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instructions for how it writes down important project knowledge have been rewritten to be clearer and easier to understand. This affects the backend logic that guides how the assistant remembers and shares key details about the codebase with future readers. If you looked at the actual prompt text, you'd see simpler wording about when and how to create knowledge files, clearer examples, and a more straightforward section on what to include or exclude.

ai.title: Fix agent loop bug and simplify tool result handling
ai.summary: Corrected strange loop bug by adding explicit end_turn instructions for terminal commands and refactoring tool result placement to avoid redundant read_file calls. Extracted simplifyReadFileToolResult helper in parse-tool-call-xml.ts to standardize file path rendering in tool results. Updated main-prompt.ts to conditionally inject tool instructions and streamline message history construction. Changes confined to backend prompt logic and XML parsing utilities.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a command and finishes, it now has a clearer signal to stop and show you the final answer instead of looping unexpectedly. File-reading results shown in conversations are also cleaned up so only the file names appear, rather than re-requesting the same file contents. This affects what you see in chat when the assistant uses tools, and it is live today.

ai.title: Discord bot auto-replies to new members in welcome channel
ai.summary: Discord bot now listens for `MessageCreate` events in the welcome channel (`1272621334580429053`) to automatically reply to system `GuildMemberJoin` messages (type 7) with instructions to use `/link`. This change requires adding `GuildMessages` and `MessageContent` intents to the client initialization. The `/link` command logic was also refactored to perform a single `select` query using `or` conditions to check for existing `discord_id` or `email` matches, replacing the previous `update` with `isNull` check, to ensure accurate validation of account linkage status before updating the database.

eli5.text: When someone new joins the Codebuff Discord server, the bot now automatically posts a helpful message in the welcome area telling them to type the link command to connect their account. The bot also got better at checking whether your email is already connected to another Discord account before letting you link, so you'll get a clearer error if there's a mismatch. If you're a new member joining today, you should see that automatic welcome reply appear right after you join.

ai.title: PostHog user identification via session email
ai.summary: Added useEffect in web/src/lib/PostHogProvider.tsx to call posthog.identify and posthog.alias when a NextAuth session is active. Uses session.user.email as the primary distinct_id while storing session.user.id as a property and creating an alias between them. Updates web/knowledge.md to document this identification strategy for consistent cross-system tracking.

eli5.text: When you sign into the app, the analytics system now ties your email address to your activity so your actions show up under one consistent profile instead of scattered across sessions. This means your usage data in PostHog (the tool that tracks how features are used) will correctly follow you across logins on the same email account. For you as a signed-in user, nothing visible changes, but the internal tracking that helps the team understand feature usage gets more accurate per person.

ai.title: Revert endturn prompt and tool result simplification changes
ai.summary: Reverts the previous fix regarding end_turn instructions and updated file placement in tool results. The change restores the original prompt logic in backend/src/main-prompt.ts and removes the simplifyReadFileToolResult export from backend/src/util/parse-tool-call-xml.ts. This rollback addresses issues introduced by the prior commit, specifically affecting how terminal command successes and file read results are communicated to the model.

eli5.text: The assistant temporarily gained new behavior for deciding when to wrap up: after a successful terminal command, it was told it could skip extra writing and end the turn, and file-read results were condensed to just show which files were read instead of their contents. That adjustment caused problems, so it has been rolled back. The assistant is back to its original instructions for ending turns and for showing file-read results, so it now talks and reports results the same way it did before.

ai.title: Log discord username on role add
ai.summary: Added discordUsername to logger.info payload in web/src/discord/client.ts. This aids debugging by capturing the username alongside userId and discordId when adding verified role. Scope limited to Discord bot client logging.

eli5.text: When the system gives someone the verified role on Discord, it now saves their Discord username in the internal logs along with their user ID. This change only affects the bot's behind-the-scenes logging and doesn't alter any user-facing behavior. If someone reviews the logs later, they'll see the actual Discord name of the person who received the role instead of just an ID number. The feature is live today.

ai.title: Revert tool result simplification and endturn logic
ai.summary: Reverts previous changes to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/util/parse-tool-call-xml.ts`. Removes `simplifyReadFileToolResult` export and restores inline simplification logic. Reinstates specific `end_turn` instruction handling for terminal commands.

eli5.text: The assistant's helper software for reading tool results was rolled back to its prior behavior. Specifically, logic that had been simplified and moved into a shared function was restored to run inline, and a rule that told the assistant to stop responding immediately after a successful terminal command was removed. If you looked at the system now, you'd see the assistant no longer receives that special instruction to end its turn right after running a command, and tool results for file reads are processed using the original inline approach rather than the extracted helper.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer mentions a list of files it says you already read earlier in the chat. When you ask it to look at files, it will only show you the files it just read, and drop the extra note it used to append saying those other files were already up to date, so the response you see is shorter and omits that repeated list. This is live today and only affects what shows up in that particular tool result, not how reading files actually works.

ai.title: Fix readfiles tool call logging and return values
ai.summary: Updated `getFileReadingUpdates` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to correctly return `addedFiles` instead of `newFiles`. Enhanced debug logging for `read_files` tool calls to include `addedFilesPaths`, `nonExistingPaths`, and `updatedFilePaths`. This resolves internal state tracking issues for file reading operations.

eli5.text: You wouldn't notice this directly, but behind the scenes, the system that tracks which files the assistant reads and remembers when those files change has been fixed. Previously, it was keeping track of new files incorrectly, which could cause it to miss updates or lose track of files it had already seen. Now it correctly records which files were read, which were new, and which ones were updated, so the assistant's memory of your files stays accurate. This is a back-end maintenance fix that improves the reliability of the file-reading feature.

ai.title: Restore mocked modules in main-prompt tests
ai.summary: Refactored `mainPrompt` tests to restore original modules after each test. Moved mocks inside `describe` block with `beforeEach` and `afterEach` hooks. Prevents mock leakage between tests.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up how the main prompt is tested, moving the fake versions of external services inside each test group and restoring the real ones after every test runs. This stops one test's fakes from leaking into another, which could otherwise make tests unreliable. You wouldn't notice this as a user, but your developers now have more trustworthy tests when they change how the assistant talks to outside services like different AI providers.

ai.summary: process-stream.ts updates parseAttributes regex to allow whitespace around equals signs. Function exported to enable direct unit testing. Tests moved to backend/src/__tests__.

eli5.text: If you write a label with extra spaces around the equals sign, like mylabel = "hello" instead of mylabel="hello", the system now reads it correctly instead of ignoring it. Tests that check this labeling behavior were reorganized into a single folder so they're easier to run and maintain. You wouldn't see any difference unless you're someone writing or checking those labels, which is mainly the internal team.

ai.title: Replace mock.module with spyOn in main-prompt tests
ai.summary: Refactored `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts` to use `spyOn` and `mock.restore` instead of manual `mock.module` swapping and restoration. This simplifies mock lifecycle management by automatically restoring original implementations after each test. The change is internal to the test suite and does not affect production code or user-facing behavior.

eli5.text: Nothing for you to see here. This was housekeeping inside the project's automated test suite, where the engineers replaced one way of faking external services (the artificial brains the software asks for help) with a newer, cleaner method that cleans itself up after each test. If you looked at the test code, you'd see the new approach makes each test set up and tear down its own pretend services automatically instead of manually swapping files before and after each test. It has no effect on how the actual product works.
